logline: A pen rides through an absurdly tidy office where machines keep producing complete-looking documents, until the hand that picks it up reveals which work is still unfinished.
angle_executed: In the KGS workflows described by AWS, the machine's finished output is still unfinished professional work.
cold_open_first_3_seconds: Extreme close-up: a fountain pen is resting across a report slot. A neatly assembled stack rises underneath and gently catapults the pen into an extravagant end-over-end pirouette. Everything lands perfectly square except the pen, which remains suspended diagonally on the stack edge. A physical OUTPUT READY sign is already steady. No face, approval stamp, stopwatch, or error alarm.

casting_shelf_first.hero: The single pen from PenAndDocument, lib/props.tsx. Promote its existing pen geometry into a reusable independently placeable pen pose if needed; do not redraw a new character.

casting_shelf_first.new_asset_budget: Zero new hero silhouettes. One bounded shelf refinement may allow the existing pen to be picked up and make a neutral editing stroke, without signature or approval animation.
casting_shelf_first.why_pen: Its unused physical tip makes the difference between produced material and remaining professional action legible without another document-as-hero film.

freshness_vs_last_two.September_12: Moves away from lilac daylight, Sheet hero and research-notebook assembly. This is a deep office stage, lateral physical comedy and one elongated pen.
freshness_vs_last_two.September_11: No medicine crate, vehicle crossing, proof lamps or rural landscape. The scene changes happen between a mailroom, a record aisle, a drafting bay and a review table.
freshness_vs_last_two.tentative_palette: Inky steel blue room, clean white stock, warm copper pen and muted aqua functional hardware. Warm desk pools within cooler office depth. Avoid the previous lilac/citron and spruce/berry combinations.

physical_sets.name: Mailroom
physical_sets.shape: Tall intake slot, low receiving counter, receding cabinet wall; the hook and email request have a real location.

physical_sets.name: Record aisle
physical_sets.shape: Cabinet canyon opened into a calm mechanical lookup cutaway; labeled API connections and PREBUILT LOGIC, not an LLM brain.

physical_sets.name: Drafting bay
physical_sets.shape: Broad shallow work surface with movable section blocks under JUMPSTARTER and LLM labels; persists FIRST DRAFT.

physical_sets.name: Review table
physical_sets.shape: Side-lit desk seen from the professional's position, with separate DORA report and Jumpstarter draft areas.

physical_sets.name: Corporate announcement foyer
physical_sets.shape: A deep wall of physical company nameplates and a small Alaska map; geography expresses ownership, not local deployment.

scenes.action: The rising report stack flips the pen into a poised balancing act; its nib still has no job. Plant the question of what will finally require it.

The pen becomes a diagonal pointer beside the September 11th KGS announcement and Wingman nameplate; contracting, logistics and financial management each get a distinct little office doorway. Corporate identity remains literal.
A neutral email-subject token marked VENDOR IDENTIFIER enters a physical slot. EARLIER ARMY PROCUREMENT and AWS CASE STUDY identify the change of time and source.

Named SAM.GOV/API connections deliver records into PREBUILT LOGIC. Cabinet drawers perform a courteous accordion motion, aligning their contents without disorder. The pen rides along a stable report rail.
DORA's material lands as a standardized report. The pen balances above the ready report without writing. The format looks genuinely useful and orderly.

A separate Jumpstarter mechanism receives user inputs and composes section blocks through Bedrock/LLM drafting. FIRST DRAFT is permanently attached. Plant whether that tag disappears when the page looks complete.

Give the opposing case its strongest picture: both useful machine outputs are present, tidy and readable as distinct object types. DORA has a record report; Jumpstarter has an editable draft. The pen bridges the two without merging their workflows.
The professional examines the DORA report and follows its organized source tabs. This is review for determination, not an award or a fabricated compliance finding. The pen is still parked.

At 90 seconds the same professional hand picks up the pen and refines a neutral draft section. The pen's long-promised job is an edit. No content is labeled false, no signature is drawn, and no decision is represented as completed.

Section blocks politely shuffle to make room for a human refinement. At 103 seconds the FIRST DRAFT tag remains visibly attached to the now-refined page. A completed-looking layout did not itself confer approval.
The pen settles as a pointer connecting KONIAG GOVERNMENT SERVICES to KONIAG and the Kodiak region. The brief scoped absence names what the current announcement does not quantify.
Match the hook's diagonal pen silhouette, now held deliberately over the work. OUTPUT READY remains true behind it. The foreground action is the professional continuing the task.

escalation: The opening has a finished machine output and a conspicuously unused pen. The fresh KGS announcement gives that office mechanism a real owner and scope. DORA turns one identifier into assembled evidence. The separate Jumpstarter mechanism changes the output into generated language before the first minute ends. Both appear complete, which makes the remaining professional work the live question.
earned_turn: A professional's work depends on what arrived. The DORA report is examined for determination; generated sections are refined and approved by people in the described workflow. The pen is not waiting for an invented failure. It has an ordinary documented task left to do.

button.line: The machine finished. Which job is still on your desk?
button.image: The opening's diagonal pen returns in the professional's grip, poised over a draft; the machine's OUTPUT READY sign stays calmly true in the distance.
button.why_it_loops: The same object and shape now have a purpose the hook withheld. Finishing the machine task remains worth crediting.

sight_gags.gag: A tidy report stack gives the pen a ludicrously elegant pirouette, then catches it by sheer office neatness.
sight_gags.target: Generic office physics; no company or person is mocked.

sight_gags.gag: Cabinet drawers open as a perfectly polite accordion; the last one tucks itself in to give the report room.
sight_gags.target: The choreography of clerical preparation, with no broken machinery.

sight_gags.gag: Generated section blocks arrive like an over-rehearsed chorus line; the FIRST DRAFT tab is the one stubbornly oversized accessory.
sight_gags.target: The visual neatness of draft output, not its accuracy.

sight_gags.gag: Draft section blocks shuffle sideways like people letting someone into a theater row, making room for the pen's small refinement.
sight_gags.target: Neutral section organization; not a fabricated correction of a model error.

act3_test.scene_name: Two Finished Outputs, Two Unfinished Jobs
act3_test.strongest_fair_case_against: The machines have really performed useful preparation. Calling the work unfinished must not make that contribution disappear or invent trouble to justify the human.
act3_test.drawn_at_full_strength: Scene 7 presents both outputs as complete, orderly and useful. Scenes 8 and 9 show the sourced next actions: examining an assembled record and refining generated sections. No error cue, review timer, bureaucratic barrier or final-award stamp supplies false tension.
act3_test.answer: The output can be ready and the professional action can still be incomplete. Different outputs call for different human work.

throughline_object.object: One copper pen from the PenAndDocument shelf rig

states.state: Unclaimed: balanced diagonally above a machine output.
Carried: rides the record rail while DORA prepares its report.
Bridging: rests between two separately labeled outputs at the Act 3 boundary.
Working: picked up for a neutral refinement of generated sections.
Owned: held deliberately through the corporate return and the button, never pretending to sign an award.

throughline_object.continuity_rule: Copper body, dark grip and one small pale barrel band remain visible at each act boundary; paper is supporting material, not the throughline hero.

loops.promise: What work will finally require the conspicuously idle pen?
loops.payoff: The professional picks it up to refine a generated section. The answer is an edit, not an automatic completion mark.

loops.promise: Will FIRST DRAFT disappear merely because all the generated sections look neatly finished?
loops.payoff: It remains visibly attached while the professional is working. Physical completeness and approval are separate.

padding_test: Cutting Scene 7 would make the back half sound dismissive of real preparation; its strong opposing picture is essential.
Cutting Scene 8 would replace the actual DORA review with a generic hand icon and lose the difference between evidence and drafting.
Cutting Scene 9 would leave the pen promise unanswered and human refinement merely asserted.
Cutting Scene 10 would allow a neat, human-touched page to read as approved; keeping FIRST DRAFT while work continues closes the second question.
A 90-second cut loses the first payoff or collapses refinement, draft status, ownership scope and button into an unreadable rush. The added time goes to distinct actions, not a review wait.

guardrails: No DORA stopwatch or portfolio dollar/hour totals.
DORA API and prebuilt-logic identity and Jumpstarter LLM identity both legible before 59 seconds.
The earlier examples are distinct, not depicted as one required serial procurement pipeline or literal Wingman architecture.
Neutral pen edits may organize an abstract section; no specific invented error, vendor outcome, legal conclusion, real UEI or private record.
FIRST DRAFT remains on every Jumpstarter document; no approval stamp, signature or final contract.
KGS and Koniag are named corporations. No Native personification, costume, cultural prop or generic Tribal framing.
Alaska return remains unquantified in this announcement; the absence does not claim no benefit.
Illustrative mechanisms are visibly sourced to AWS, and the fresh announcement remains distinct.
